players.product: server CPU LGA sockets and high-speed connectors

quarterly_data.signal: Lotes Q1 2026 results (Citi Taiwan Tech Conference deck): quarterly revenue NT$9,328 million (Q4'25: NT$9,261 million; Q1'25: NT$7,765 million); gross margin 49.55%; operating margin 29.04%; net profit NT$2,433 million; EPS NT$21.37. Full-year 2025 revenue NT$33,783 million and EPS NT$70.17.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2025 revenue NT$33,783 million; FY2025 EPS NT$70.17 (Q1'26 values in the signal; the deck's quarterly table text is extracted without separators)

quarterly_data.signal: Business coverage slide: the revenue line whose current main products are CPU sockets, DDR and PCIe connectors rose to 51.02% of revenue in Q1'26, from 39.56% in 2025, 34.1% in 2024 and 26~27% in 2023; its future product plan lists CPU socket, HSIO & cable, SOCAMM and QDs. Lotes describes itself as a worldwide top 3 CPU socket supplier selected by many customers as their strategic partner, giving it more chances to co-develop front-end products.
quarterly_data.figure: CPU socket / DDR / PCIe line 51.02% of Q1'26 revenue (39.56% in 2025)

quarterly_data.signal: Lotes' product roadmap slide lists the socket vendors per CPU platform: Intel Server - LOTES, FIT, TE; Intel Desktop - LOTES, FIT, Deren; AMD Server - LOTES, FIT (Milan), LOTES, FIT, Amphenol (Genoa), LOTES, FIT, TE (Venice, SP7(7536) / SP8(5572)); AMD Desktop - LOTES, FIT; Altra (4926), Siryn (5964) and Banshee (7228) also appear on the roadmap. The slide notes that products with color unfilled are still under development or time to market unknown.
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: customer (server CPU sockets, per the vendor roadmap)
